messages:
Ana (Docs): heads-up — PR #3421 updated the Python streaming example in streaming.md but I just noticed it never awaits the async iterator close. Clients can leak sockets.
Mike H: oh no, repro?
Ana (Docs): minimal repro: async for chunk in client.stream_gen(prompt):
  print(chunk)
# but there's no explicit close and our generator uses background tasks so process sticks around sometimes.
Sophia L: ugh, thanks for catching. We should either demonstrate usage with 'async with' or call client.close() at the end.
Ana (Docs): I drafted a quick patch to switch to an async context manager:

```py
async with client.stream(prompt) as stream:
  async for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk)
# client closed automatically
```

Can someone sanity-check? I want to avoid breaking older patterns in the snippet.
Mike H: that looks good. We should add a one-liner comment about older SDK versions not supporting context manager and include the fallback.
Juan P: for Go pagination examples I noticed PR #3421 changed the cursor lifetime incorrectly — nil cursor was being passed through, causing server to return first page repeatedly. We should show how to persist cursor across calls.
Ana (Docs): can you paste the Go diff here?
Juan P: sure — current snippet does: 

```go
resp, _ := client.List(ctx, &ListOptions{})
for resp.HasMore() {
  resp, _ = client.List(ctx, resp.NextCursor())
}
```

But resp.NextCursor() returned "" on some backends; need to check for empty and stop.

Suggest: 
```go
resp, _ := client.List(ctx, &ListOptions{})
for {
  if !resp.HasMore() || resp.NextCursor() == "" {
    break
  }
  resp, _ = client.List(ctx, resp.NextCursor())
}
```

Kate R: also add small bit about deterministic page size and timeouts. Otherwise users hit accidental infinite loops with buggy servers.
Sophia L: TS side: the retry example uses an exponential backoff util but we didn't set maxDelay, so folks could wait minutes. I propose an opinionated snippet: retry with base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s, and show abort after 6 attempts.
Ana (Docs): good idea. Draft for TS: 

```ts
const retry = backoff({ base: 200, factor: 2, max: 5000, attempts: 6 });
await sdk.call({ prompt }, { retry });
```

Add note: "these knobs trade total latency for success rate; tune per workload."
Mike H: small docs nit — streaming.md still links to the old "function-calling v1" doc. Link should point to /docs/functions/calling-v2 (we changed route in the API release).
Ana (Docs): I will update links. DevX Bot, can you run link-check on the branch?
DevX Bot: running link-check on branch docs/stream-fixes (#3421)...
DevX Bot: found 1 broken link: /docs/functions/calling-v1 -> 404. Suggested replacement: /docs/functions/calling-v2.
DevX Bot: lint OK, spellcheck: warning on "repro" (accepted).
Ana (Docs): thanks — I've pushed fixes: switched Python snippet to async context manager, added fallback snippet with client.close(), updated Go pagination logic, added TS retry params, fixed link to calling-v2, and added a short blurb about context managers and resource cleanup.
Juan P: can we also add a brief test snippet for the Go example that simulates empty cursor to ensure docs code doesn't loop? A 3-line test would give confidence.
Kate R: agree, simple unit test is good — add to examples_test.go next to other pagination tests.
Sophia L: PR updated with tests and examples. Requesting review from @Mike H and @Juan P.
Mike H: reviewing now. Quick thumbs-up if CI passes. :thumbsup:
Ana (Docs): thanks team. After merge I'll add a short note in the changelog and ping the SDK teams to backport to the v0.x branch if feasible.
Mike H: one last tiny ask — make the Python snippet explicitly import 'asyncio' in the example file to avoid confusion in copy-paste.
Ana (Docs): done. Pushed again.
DevX Bot: CI passed, link-check passed, docs build succeeded.
Mike H: landed as #3421. Nice catch, Ana.
Ana (Docs): thanks all — closing thread. If anyone sees more streaming edgecases, drop here or open a tiny PR. :sparkles:
